quiz.title: Class 12 Maths Case Study Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight CBSE-style case study questions across calculus, matrices, probability, 3D geometry and linear programming. Read each short scenario, pick an answer, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A tin maker builds an open box from an 18 cm square sheet by cutting equal squares of side x cm from the corners and folding up the sides, giving volume V(x) = x(18 − 2x)². For what x is the volume greatest?
questions.explanation: V'(x) = (18 − 2x)(18 − 6x). Setting it to zero gives x = 9 (a minimum, box collapses) or x = 3. The second-derivative test confirms x = 3 cm is the maximum.

questions.q: A spherical weather balloon is inflated so its radius grows at 0.5 cm/s. Using dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt), how fast is the volume rising when the radius is 7 cm?
A school orders x cricket bats and y balls. The count gives x + y = 30 and the cost gives 2x + y = 40, written as [[1,1],[2,1]][x;y] = [30;40]. What is the determinant of the coefficient matrix?
questions.explanation: The determinant is (1)(1) − (1)(2) = 1 − 2 = −1. It is non-zero, so the system has a unique solution.

questions.q: Solving the same order system x + y = 30 and 2x + y = 40, how many bats (x) did the school buy?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the first equation from the second: (2x + y) − (x + y) = 40 − 30, so x = 10 (and y = 20).

questions.q: A plant runs machines A and B. A makes 60% of bolts, B makes 40%; 2% of A's and 5% of B's bolts are defective. A bolt is found defective. By Bayes' theorem, what is the probability it came from B?
questions.explanation: P(B and defective) = 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.02; total defective = 0.6 × 0.02 + 0.02 = 0.032. So P(B | defective) = 0.02 / 0.032 = 5/8.

questions.q: A student guesses on a 5-question true/false test, each answer correct with probability 1/2 independently. Using the binomial distribution, what is P(exactly 3 correct)?
A drone sits at the point (1, 2, 3). A flat camera panel lies on the plane 2x − y + 2z = 15. What is the shortest distance from the drone to the panel?

A bakery makes x cakes (profit ₹80 each) and y cookie batches (profit ₹30 each). Its feasible corner points are (0,0), (20,0), (12,16) and (0,24). Maximising Z = 80x + 30y, which corner gives the most profit?

faq.q: What are case study questions in Class 12 maths?
faq.a: They are questions that open with a short real-world scenario — a box being cut, a balloon inflating, a factory's defect rate — and then ask sub-questions that test the underlying concept. CBSE includes them to check whether you can apply a method, not just recall a formula.

faq.q: Which chapters do Class 12 case studies usually cover?
faq.a: The most common are applications of derivatives (maxima, minima and rates), matrices and determinants, probability (Bayes' theorem and binomial), three-dimensional geometry, and linear programming. These carry the bulk of the application-based marks in the board paper.

faq.q: How many marks do case study questions carry in the CBSE Class 12 exam?
faq.a: The paper typically has case-based questions worth 4 marks each, usually split into smaller parts. They reward students who read the scenario carefully and set up the right equation before calculating.

faq.q: How should I approach a case study question in the exam?
faq.a: Read the scenario twice, write down the given data and what is asked, then match it to a standard method — optimisation, a matrix equation, Bayes' theorem, a distance formula or an LPP corner check. Solving the setup correctly is worth more than rushing to an answer.
